items.title: Roger Kellaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: from Shearing it went on to Billy Taylor, and then Oscar Peterson

ctx.x: Well let me comment on a few things that I have read and you can tell me if they’re accurate or not — that some of your jazz interest came from hearing George Shearing?

George Shearing was my very first influence. I used to play “I’ll Remember April,” which his arrangement came out in sheet music. And when I was 13 — I started crossing over into jazz when I was around that age — and I was a professional at 14. But prior to that I was playing that piece. That was my favorite piece of music. I love those early solo © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

things of George’s and from Shearing it went on to Billy Taylor, and then Oscar Peterson and then Horace Silver. And in the interim, Fats Waller was mixed in with all of that. Fats more than any of the others, more than James P. Johnson or any of the others. Jimmy Yancy is a boogie piano player that I came across in the 60s when I was working for a copyist. I had to do some takedowns and I discovered him.
